questions.competency: I.A — Professional Ethics, Core Security Concepts, and Governance Principles
questions.skill: Managing a professional conflict of interest ethically
questions.performanceIndicator: Disclose competing interests before accepting work that could impair professional judgment
questions.scenarioContext: A security architect is asked to evaluate proposals for a major contract. One bidder employs the architect's spouse, and the architect could influence the selection even though the spouse is not on the proposal team.
questions.prompt: What should the security architect do FIRST?

choices.A: Disclose the relationship through the appropriate channel and follow the organization's recusal decision
choices.B: Remain on the evaluation because the spouse did not write the proposal
choices.C: Privately favor another bidder so no one suspects a conflict
choices.D: Share proposal details with the spouse to confirm that no conflict exists

questions.explanation: Prompt disclosure allows the organization to assess the actual or perceived conflict and decide whether recusal or another safeguard is required. The absence of direct proposal work does not remove the appearance of impaired judgment. Secretly favoring another bidder is still biased, and sharing confidential proposal information would create an additional ethical and contractual problem.

questions.competency: I.A — Professional Ethics, Core Security Concepts, and Governance Principles
questions.skill: Identifying loss of availability in a critical business service
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply the CIA triad to an interruption without disclosure or modification
questions.scenarioContext: A ticketing service contains accurate data and no customer information is exposed, but legitimate users cannot access the service during a prolonged outage.
questions.prompt: Which security objective is MOST directly affected?

choices.A: Authenticity
choices.B: Confidentiality
choices.C: Availability
choices.D: Integrity

questions.explanation: Availability ensures that authorized users can obtain systems and information when needed. The outage directly violates that objective even though the records remain accurate and undisclosed. Confidentiality concerns exposure, integrity concerns unauthorized change, and authenticity concerns whether an identity or item is genuine.

questions.competency: I.A — Professional Ethics, Core Security Concepts, and Governance Principles
questions.skill: Defining board-level oversight of enterprise security risk
questions.performanceIndicator: Distinguish governing oversight from operational security management
questions.scenarioContext: The board of a regional utility receives detailed vulnerability reports but has no clear view of security risk relative to business objectives, legal duties, or approved risk appetite.
questions.prompt: Which change would BEST strengthen the board's governance role?

choices.A: Have the board approve individual firewall rules for critical systems
choices.B: Transfer accountability for enterprise risk to the security operations manager
choices.C: Ask directors to investigate every security alert personally
choices.D: Provide decision-focused reporting on material risk, appetite exceptions, accountability, and treatment progress

questions.explanation: The board provides direction and oversight by understanding material exposure, monitoring performance against risk appetite, and holding management accountable. Firewall rules and alert investigations are operational matters. Delegating enterprise accountability to an operations manager would place a governance responsibility at the wrong organizational level.

questions.competency: I.A — Professional Ethics, Core Security Concepts, and Governance Principles
questions.skill: Selecting indicators that demonstrate security governance effectiveness
questions.performanceIndicator: Differentiate decision-oriented governance measures from raw operational activity
questions.prompt: Senior leaders want evidence that security governance is influencing accountable business decisions. Which 2 measures would provide the MOST relevant evidence? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: The total number of log entries generated by all systems
choices.B: The percentage of material risks with an assigned business owner and approved treatment decision
choices.C: The number of pages in the security policy manual
choices.D: The number of tools operated by the security team
choices.E: The trend in risk-appetite exceptions that remain unresolved beyond approved deadlines

questions.explanation: Assigned business ownership and approved treatment decisions show that governance is producing accountable action. Trends in overdue appetite exceptions reveal whether escalated risks are being resolved. Log volume, policy length, and tool count measure activity or scale but do not demonstrate that leaders are making and enforcing risk decisions.

questions.competency: I.A — Professional Ethics, Core Security Concepts, and Governance Principles
questions.skill: Establishing security accountability in a joint venture
questions.performanceIndicator: Define shared governance before connecting systems and exchanging sensitive information
questions.scenarioContext: Two construction firms form a joint venture and plan to connect selected services. Each firm assumes the other will manage security incidents, approve access, and accept risks involving the shared environment.
questions.prompt: What should the venture's steering group establish before the connection is activated?

choices.A: A rule that whichever firm discovers a problem automatically accepts all related risk
choices.B: Documented decision rights, control responsibilities, incident duties, escalation paths, and risk ownership
choices.C: A shared administrator account so both firms have equal technical authority
choices.D: Separate technical standards with no process for resolving conflicts

questions.explanation: Shared operations require explicit governance so each party knows who decides, implements, monitors, reports, escalates, and accepts risk. Discovery does not determine ownership, a shared account weakens accountability, and incompatible standards without dispute resolution leave important responsibilities unresolved.

questions.competency: I.A — Professional Ethics, Core Security Concepts, and Governance Principles
questions.skill: Tailoring a control baseline according to organizational risk
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply a security control framework without treating its baseline as inflexible
questions.scenarioContext: A museum adopts a recognized control framework. The implementation team proposes applying every control identically to public kiosks, administrative systems, and high-value collection records without considering different threats or impacts.
questions.prompt: How should the security manager respond?

choices.A: Tailor the baseline using documented risk, applicable obligations, system context, and approved exceptions
choices.B: Reject the framework because no baseline can support different environments
choices.C: Let individual administrators omit controls without documenting the decision
choices.D: Apply controls only after a system experiences a confirmed incident

questions.explanation: A control framework supplies a structured baseline that should be tailored through a documented, risk-based process. Relevant obligations and system context influence selection and strength, while exceptions require authorization. Rejecting the framework loses its governance value, informal omissions defeat consistency, and waiting for incidents is reactive rather than risk-based.

questions.competency: I.B — Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Issues, Investigations, and the Policy Hierarchy
questions.skill: Recognizing an administrative or regulatory proceeding
questions.performanceIndicator: Distinguish agency enforcement from criminal prosecution and private civil litigation
questions.scenarioContext: A licensing authority alleges that a regulated organization failed to meet mandatory security requirements. The authority can impose a monetary penalty and restrict the organization's license after an agency hearing.
questions.prompt: How should this proceeding be classified?

choices.A: A private contractual arbitration
choices.B: A criminal prosecution seeking imprisonment
choices.C: An administrative or regulatory enforcement action
choices.D: An internal personnel investigation

questions.explanation: An agency enforcing mandatory requirements through its hearing and licensing authority is conducting an administrative or regulatory action. Monetary or licensing consequences do not automatically make the matter criminal. The proceeding is neither a private dispute nor an employer's internal personnel inquiry.

questions.competency: I.B — Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Issues, Investigations, and the Policy Hierarchy
questions.skill: Using guidelines to provide flexible security recommendations
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose the policy-hierarchy document appropriate for nonmandatory advice
questions.scenarioContext: A professional association has a mandatory remote-work standard. It also wants to publish optional examples that employees may adapt to improve privacy when working in varied home environments.
questions.prompt: Which document type is MOST appropriate for the optional examples?

choices.A: Policy
choices.B: Procedure
choices.C: Standard
choices.D: Guideline

questions.explanation: A guideline supplies recommended, adaptable practices where flexibility is appropriate. A policy states management direction, a standard establishes mandatory measurable requirements, and a procedure defines required steps for performing a task. Making optional examples a guideline preserves their intended advisory character.

questions.competency: I.B — Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Issues, Investigations, and the Policy Hierarchy
questions.skill: Obtaining proper authorization and scope for an internal investigation
questions.performanceIndicator: Establish investigative authority before collecting employee information
questions.scenarioContext: A security analyst receives an informal request from a department manager to examine an employee's messages and personal storage area for possible misconduct. No case has been opened, and the analyst cannot confirm the manager's authority or the lawful scope of the search.
questions.prompt: What should the analyst do FIRST?

choices.A: Collect everything immediately so no information can be removed
choices.B: Confirm authorization, purpose, scope, privacy constraints, and required coordination before collecting evidence
choices.C: Warn the employee and ask for permission to search all available records
choices.D: Copy only the records the department manager expects will prove misconduct

questions.explanation: An internal investigation must begin with legitimate authority, defined purpose and scope, and coordination with appropriate legal, human resources, privacy, or management functions. Immediate or selective collection without that foundation can exceed authority and compromise fairness. Informing the subject prematurely may also jeopardize an authorized inquiry.

questions.competency: I.B — Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Issues, Investigations, and the Policy Hierarchy
questions.skill: Managing software license and redistribution obligations
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify governance controls needed for lawful software use and distribution
questions.scenarioContext: A product team uses proprietary development tools and incorporates externally licensed components into software distributed to customers. Management wants to reduce licensing and intellectual property exposure.
questions.prompt: Which 2 actions should the organization prioritize? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Maintain an inventory of licenses, entitlements, component terms, and approved uses
choices.B: Assume downloaded components are unrestricted if no purchase was required
choices.C: Let each developer interpret redistribution terms without review or documentation
choices.D: Review distribution obligations and approvals before releasing software containing licensed components
choices.E: Remove ownership notices so customers cannot identify third-party material

questions.explanation: An accurate license and component inventory shows what the organization may use and under which terms. Pre-release review verifies redistribution, notice, attribution, source, or other obligations before delivery. Free acquisition does not imply unrestricted rights, undocumented individual interpretation creates inconsistency, and removing required notices can violate license terms.

questions.competency: I.B — Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Issues, Investigations, and the Policy Hierarchy
questions.skill: Applying data minimization to a new personal-data collection
questions.performanceIndicator: Limit collection to information necessary for a defined and lawful purpose
questions.scenarioContext: A fitness center designs a visitor registration form. The business purpose requires a visitor's name, host, and time of entry, but the proposed form also collects birth date, government identifier, medical history, and family contacts without a defined use.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST privacy-oriented recommendation?

choices.A: Collect only data necessary for the defined purpose and document retention and access requirements
choices.B: Collect all proposed fields because future uses may emerge
choices.C: Retain every visitor record indefinitely to avoid inconsistent deletion
choices.D: Publish the collected information so visitors can verify their entries

questions.explanation: Data minimization limits collection to information necessary for a specified purpose and reduces legal and security exposure. Retention and access should also be defined. Speculative future value does not justify excessive collection, indefinite retention increases risk, and public disclosure would conflict with the privacy interests involved.

questions.competency: I.B — Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Issues, Investigations, and the Policy Hierarchy
questions.skill: Coordinating jurisdictional response to suspected cybercrime
questions.performanceIndicator: Preserve evidence and obtain legal direction before external investigative action
questions.scenarioContext: A multinational shipping company finds evidence that an external actor used infrastructure in several countries to steal funds. Executives want the internal team to contact every foreign service provider and demand account contents immediately.
questions.prompt: Which response is MOST appropriate?

choices.A: Direct employees to access the suspected foreign accounts using recovered credentials
choices.B: Publish all indicators and employee records before validating the evidence
choices.C: Preserve evidence and coordinate with counsel and authorized authorities on jurisdiction, process, and lawful requests
choices.D: Abandon the investigation because more than one country is involved

questions.explanation: Cross-border cybercrime requires preservation and coordinated legal analysis so requests, investigative actions, and disclosures follow applicable jurisdiction and authority. Unauthorized account access could itself be unlawful, premature publication may damage the case and privacy, and multiple jurisdictions make coordination more important rather than making investigation impossible.

questions.competency: I.C — Risk Management Concepts, Threat Modeling, and Supply Chain Risk
questions.skill: Deriving annualized rate of occurrence from expected frequency
questions.performanceIndicator: Convert a multi-year event estimate into an annual rate for quantitative analysis
questions.prompt: An illustrative risk assessment estimates that a specific loss event will occur once every five years. What annualized rate of occurrence should be used?
questions.explanation: One expected occurrence over five years corresponds to an annualized rate of 1 ÷ 5, or 0.20. A rate of 1.0 would imply one event per year, while 5.0 would imply five events per year. The 0.05 value would correspond to one event every twenty years.

questions.competency: I.C — Risk Management Concepts, Threat Modeling, and Supply Chain Risk
questions.skill: Governing temporary risk acceptance through a documented exception
questions.performanceIndicator: Set ownership, compensating measures, expiration, and review for time-limited acceptance
questions.scenarioContext: A manufacturing system cannot meet a new security standard until a scheduled replacement in four months. The accountable owner believes the residual exposure can be tolerated temporarily, but the exception request has no end date or interim safeguards.
questions.prompt: What should risk management require before approval?

choices.A: Permanent acceptance because replacement funding is already approved
choices.B: Documented residual risk, authorized ownership, compensating measures, a fixed expiration, and review criteria
choices.C: Removal of the risk from reporting while the exception remains active
choices.D: Approval by the system administrator who will operate the compensating controls

questions.explanation: A temporary exception should be an explicit, authorized risk decision with defined residual exposure, interim protection, accountability, expiration, and review. Approved future work does not justify permanent acceptance. The risk must remain visible, and the administrator implementing controls is not necessarily authorized to accept the business impact.

questions.competency: I.C — Risk Management Concepts, Threat Modeling, and Supply Chain Risk
questions.skill: Creating an actionable risk register entry
questions.performanceIndicator: Record cause, event, impact, ownership, treatment, and status for governance use
questions.scenarioContext: A public library's risk register contains an entry labeled only 'cyberattack — high.' Leaders cannot determine what might happen, why it matters, who owns it, or what action is underway.
questions.prompt: Which improvement would make the entry MOST useful?

choices.A: Describe the threat and vulnerability, business impact, likelihood, owner, treatment, due date, and residual risk
choices.B: Replace the entry with a list of every security product in use
choices.C: Keep the description brief and ask leaders to infer the affected objective
choices.D: Record only risks that have already produced a financial loss

questions.explanation: An actionable risk entry explains the causal scenario and business consequence, records assessment results, assigns an accountable owner, and tracks treatment and residual exposure. A tool inventory does not describe risk, vague labels prevent informed decisions, and limiting the register to realized losses excludes forward-looking risk management.

questions.competency: I.C — Risk Management Concepts, Threat Modeling, and Supply Chain Risk
questions.skill: Classifying information disclosure and elevation-of-privilege threats with STRIDE
questions.performanceIndicator: Map confidentiality exposure and unauthorized privilege gain to threat categories
questions.prompt: A threat-modeling team identifies one path that exposes confidential records to an unauthorized user and another that lets a standard user gain administrator capabilities. Which 2 STRIDE categories apply? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Tampering
choices.B: Information disclosure
choices.C: Repudiation
choices.D: Denial of service
choices.E: Elevation of privilege

questions.explanation: Unauthorized exposure of confidential records is information disclosure, and gaining administrator capabilities beyond an authorized role is elevation of privilege. Tampering concerns modification, repudiation concerns denial of an action, and denial of service concerns impaired availability rather than the behaviors described.

questions.competency: I.C — Risk Management Concepts, Threat Modeling, and Supply Chain Risk
questions.skill: Managing concentration risk across critical suppliers
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify common dependencies that can defeat apparent vendor diversification
questions.scenarioContext: An online education company uses three separate service providers for critical functions and assumes this provides resilience. A review finds that all three depend on the same underlying infrastructure operator in one region.
questions.prompt: What should the risk manager do NEXT?

choices.A: Close the review because three signed contracts prove adequate diversification
choices.B: Ask each provider to conceal its dependencies from the others
choices.C: Assess the common dependency and evaluate geographic, contractual, and recovery alternatives
choices.D: Transfer all continuity accountability to the provider with the largest contract

questions.explanation: Multiple direct vendors can still create concentration risk when they share a critical dependency. The organization should assess the combined exposure and consider realistic alternatives, recovery provisions, and geographic diversity. Contract count alone does not establish resilience, secrecy does not reduce dependency, and outsourcing does not transfer the customer's continuity accountability.

questions.competency: I.C — Risk Management Concepts, Threat Modeling, and Supply Chain Risk
questions.skill: Planning secure exit from a third-party service
questions.performanceIndicator: Include data disposition, transition support, access removal, and assurance in vendor governance
questions.scenarioContext: A property management firm is about to sign a long-term service agreement. The provider meets current security requirements, but the draft contract says nothing about transition assistance, data return, deletion, or access revocation when the relationship ends.
questions.prompt: Which action is MOST appropriate before signing?

choices.A: Defer exit planning because termination conditions cannot be known in advance
choices.B: Rely on the provider's normal practices without making them contractual
choices.C: Require the customer to abandon all historical data if the service ends
choices.D: Add enforceable exit terms covering transition, data return and verified deletion, access removal, retention duties, and cooperation

questions.explanation: Exit requirements should be agreed while the customer has negotiating leverage. Clear terms preserve continuity, govern data disposition, terminate access, respect retention obligations, and define provider cooperation. Deferring or relying on undocumented practices leaves material exposure unresolved, while abandoning required business data may create operational and legal harm.

questions.competency: I.D — Business Continuity, Personnel Security, and Security Awareness Programs
questions.skill: Interpreting a recovery point objective
questions.performanceIndicator: Relate allowable data loss to the timing of recoverable information
questions.scenarioContext: A claims process has a recovery point objective of two hours. After an interruption, the latest usable data copy is from 30 minutes before the failure.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion is MOST accurate?

choices.A: The recovery time objective has been exceeded by 90 minutes
choices.B: The available copy is within the stated tolerance for data loss
choices.C: The process may remain unavailable for exactly two hours
choices.D: No transaction reconstruction can be required because a copy exists

questions.explanation: A two-hour recovery point objective permits restoration to a point no more than two hours before the disruption. A copy from 30 minutes before the failure is within that tolerance. RPO does not define restoration duration, and transactions after the recovery point may still require reconstruction or reconciliation.

questions.competency: I.D — Business Continuity, Personnel Security, and Security Awareness Programs
questions.skill: Defining continuing security obligations in employment agreements
questions.performanceIndicator: Establish confidentiality and asset-handling duties before personnel receive access
questions.scenarioContext: A biotech startup gives researchers access to confidential methods and partner information. Its employment agreement discusses salary and leave but does not address confidentiality, acceptable use, intellectual property, or duties after employment ends.
questions.prompt: What should management do before granting access?

choices.A: Add legally reviewed, role-appropriate terms covering security responsibilities and continuing obligations
choices.B: Rely solely on verbal reminders because written terms can reduce trust
choices.C: Wait until an employee resigns before explaining confidentiality duties
choices.D: Use a technical access control as a substitute for employment terms

questions.explanation: Personnel should understand documented, lawful, and role-appropriate obligations before receiving sensitive access, including duties that survive departure where applicable. Verbal reminders are difficult to enforce consistently, post-resignation notice is too late, and technical controls complement rather than replace employment and confidentiality terms.

questions.competency: I.D — Business Continuity, Personnel Security, and Security Awareness Programs
questions.skill: Coordinating response to potential insider-risk indicators
questions.performanceIndicator: Use authorized cross-functional review instead of unilateral surveillance or accusation
questions.scenarioContext: A supervisor reports several concerning but inconclusive behaviors by an employee with sensitive access. The behaviors may have innocent explanations, and the organization has an established insider-risk process involving security, human resources, legal counsel, and management.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST next step?

choices.A: Publicly confront the employee so coworkers can provide additional allegations
choices.B: Ignore the report until a confirmed loss occurs
choices.C: Refer the facts through the authorized process for proportionate, documented, and lawful assessment
choices.D: Begin unrestricted monitoring of the employee's personal accounts

questions.explanation: A cross-functional insider-risk process enables proportionate assessment, protects confidentiality and fairness, and ensures that monitoring or employment actions have proper authority. Public accusation can cause harm and compromise review, waiting for loss is unnecessarily reactive, and unrestricted personal surveillance may exceed lawful and organizational authority.

questions.competency: I.D — Business Continuity, Personnel Security, and Security Awareness Programs
questions.skill: Identifying events that require continuity plan maintenance
questions.performanceIndicator: Trigger plan review when material organizational or process assumptions change
questions.prompt: Which 2 events should MOST clearly trigger review and update of affected business continuity plans? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: A critical business process moves to a new facility and changes key suppliers
choices.B: A department changes the color scheme of an internal presentation template
choices.C: A merger changes process ownership, staffing, systems, and recovery dependencies
choices.D: An employee corrects a spelling error in a noncritical newsletter
choices.E: A team holds its regular meeting in a different conference room

questions.explanation: Relocation with supplier changes and a merger that alters ownership, people, systems, and dependencies can invalidate recovery assumptions and therefore require plan maintenance. Cosmetic document edits, routine room changes, and unrelated spelling corrections do not materially change continuity requirements.

questions.competency: I.D — Business Continuity, Personnel Security, and Security Awareness Programs
questions.skill: Distinguishing security awareness, training, and education
questions.performanceIndicator: Match a long-term professional development need to security education
questions.scenarioContext: An organization wants selected employees to develop broad, in-depth security knowledge for future professional roles, beyond immediate task instruction or short messages intended to influence daily behavior.
questions.prompt: Which type of learning activity BEST fits this objective?

choices.A: A brief awareness reminder about reporting suspicious messages
choices.B: A procedural demonstration for performing one assigned security task
choices.C: A compliance acknowledgment with no instructional content
choices.D: A structured security education program that develops broad knowledge over time

questions.explanation: Education develops broad conceptual knowledge and professional capability over an extended period. Awareness focuses attention and behavior, while training builds skills for particular duties or tasks. Acknowledgment may document receipt of a requirement but does not itself meet the stated learning objective.

questions.competency: I.D — Business Continuity, Personnel Security, and Security Awareness Programs
questions.skill: Reducing key-person dependency in business continuity planning
questions.performanceIndicator: Establish alternate personnel and usable documentation for critical activities
questions.scenarioContext: A community bank discovers that only one employee knows how to complete a time-sensitive settlement process during a system disruption. The recovery plan lists that employee by name but provides no alternate or documented workaround.
questions.prompt: Which action would BEST reduce the continuity risk?

choices.A: Increase the employee's normal workload so the process is completed faster
choices.B: Document the recovery procedure, cross-train authorized alternates, and exercise the arrangement
choices.C: Remove the process from the continuity plan because it depends on one person
choices.D: Assume the employee will remain reachable during every disruption

questions.explanation: Documented procedures, trained alternates, and exercises reduce key-person dependency and demonstrate that the workaround is usable. More routine workload does not create resilience, removing a time-sensitive process hides the risk, and relying on one person's availability leaves the original single point of failure unchanged.

questions.competency: II.A — Classifying and Handling Information and Assets
questions.skill: Classifying derived analytical assets
questions.performanceIndicator: Assess a derived asset according to the sensitivity and business impact of the information it reveals
questions.scenarioContext: A consumer-lending company builds a forecasting model from several internal datasets. The model does not contain complete source records, but its parameters and outputs can reveal confidential pricing strategy and patterns about high-value customer segments.
questions.prompt: How should the model be classified?

choices.A: As public, because the model does not contain complete source records
choices.B: According to the sensitivity and business impact of what the model and its outputs can reveal
choices.C: At the same level as the least sensitive source dataset used for training
choices.D: Only after an external party demonstrates that confidential information can be inferred

questions.explanation: A derived analytical asset should be classified according to the information it exposes and the impact of unauthorized disclosure, alteration, or loss. The absence of complete source records does not make the model public. Using the least sensitive input understates risk, and waiting for demonstrated external inference is reactive rather than risk-based.

questions.competency: II.A — Classifying and Handling Information and Assets
questions.skill: Applying handling requirements to spoken information
questions.performanceIndicator: Extend classification-based safeguards to conversations and other non-digital forms
questions.scenarioContext: Executives at a food-distribution company plan to discuss a confidential acquisition during a conference. The reserved room has thin partitions, visitors use the adjacent space, and notes from prior meetings remain on a whiteboard.
questions.prompt: Which action BEST satisfies the handling requirement?

choices.A: Proceed because classification labels apply only to recorded information.
choices.B: Ask attendees to speak quietly and erase the whiteboard after the discussion.
choices.C: Hold the meeting as planned but prohibit attendees from taking written notes.
choices.D: Move the discussion to an approved private location and clear residual information before and after use.

questions.explanation: Handling obligations follow confidential information regardless of whether it is digital, printed, written on a board, or spoken. An approved private location and removal of residual information address both eavesdropping and visual exposure. Speaking quietly or restricting notes does not adequately control the environment.

questions.competency: II.A — Classifying and Handling Information and Assets
questions.skill: Resolving ownership gaps before classification decisions
questions.performanceIndicator: Escalate unowned assets for accountable ownership assignment rather than allowing custodians to assume business authority
questions.scenarioContext: During an inventory review, a cloud operations team finds a repository containing years of partner performance data. The original business unit was dissolved, no successor owner is documented, and the operations team cannot determine whether a new analytics request is an authorized use.
questions.prompt: What should the cloud custodian do FIRST?

choices.A: Escalate the ownership gap so an accountable business owner can be assigned before use and classification decisions are made.
choices.B: Approve the analytics request because custodians control the repository.
choices.C: Delete the repository immediately because every asset must have a current owner.
choices.D: Allow read-only access while waiting for a future organizational restructuring.

questions.explanation: The custodian should preserve the asset and escalate the missing accountability so an authorized business owner can determine classification, permitted use, and disposition. Operating the repository does not grant business decision authority. Immediate deletion may violate retention needs, while provisional access could enable an unauthorized secondary use.

questions.competency: II.A — Classifying and Handling Information and Assets
questions.skill: Selecting labels that communicate handling requirements
questions.performanceIndicator: Use clear, consistent marking to make required handling evident to authorized users
questions.scenarioContext: A mining company uses four information classifications, but departments display different abbreviations and colors for the same level. Employees transferring between sites frequently misinterpret which sharing and storage rules apply.
questions.prompt: Which improvement would MOST directly reduce the handling errors?

choices.A: Allow each site to keep local markings and publish a yearly comparison chart.
choices.B: Replace classification markings with the name of the department that created the information.
choices.C: Standardize labels and associate each label with centrally defined handling requirements.
choices.D: Remove visible labels and rely on users to determine sensitivity from context.

questions.explanation: Consistent labels tied to defined handling rules give users a common, actionable indication of how assets must be protected. Local variations preserve ambiguity, department names do not express sensitivity, and removing labels forces subjective decisions that increase inconsistent handling.

questions.competency: II.A — Classifying and Handling Information and Assets
questions.skill: Reviewing classification after material business changes
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify events that require an owner-led reassessment of classification and handling
questions.scenarioContext: A medical-device manufacturer is reviewing information assets after selling one product line and entering a new jurisdiction. Some records have lost operational value, while others are now subject to additional disclosure and handling obligations.
questions.prompt: Which TWO actions are most appropriate? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Keep every existing classification unchanged to preserve consistency over time.
choices.B: Have accountable owners reassess affected assets against current sensitivity, criticality, and obligations.
choices.C: Let custodians lower classifications whenever storage costs increase.
choices.D: Update handling requirements and labels when the approved reassessment changes an asset's classification.
choices.E: Apply the highest classification to every record associated with both product lines.

questions.explanation: Material changes in business use and legal context warrant an owner-led reassessment, followed by updated labels and handling rules when the classification changes. Freezing all classifications ignores current risk, custodians should not downgrade assets for cost reasons, and classifying everything at the highest level creates unnecessary restrictions without a risk-based basis.

questions.competency: II.B — Secure Provisioning and Asset Retention
questions.skill: Provisioning ephemeral cloud resources with lifecycle controls
questions.performanceIndicator: Ensure temporary virtual assets have approved configurations, accountable ownership, inventory visibility, and automatic expiration
questions.scenarioContext: A software company allows development teams to create temporary cloud environments for testing. Many environments lack an owner tag, use inconsistent configurations, and continue running months after the associated projects end.
questions.prompt: Which control would BEST address the lifecycle weakness?

choices.A: Provision environments through approved templates that require ownership, inventory registration, and expiration metadata.
choices.B: Allow unrestricted creation but ask teams to review their resources once a year.
choices.C: Increase the cloud budget so abandoned environments do not affect active projects.
choices.D: Exclude temporary resources from asset management because they are not physical devices.

questions.explanation: Temporary virtual resources remain organizational assets and need secure, accountable provisioning. Approved templates combined with required ownership, inventory, and expiration data enable consistent deployment and timely retirement. Annual review is too slow, additional budget does not reduce exposure, and excluding virtual assets creates unmanaged infrastructure.

questions.competency: II.B — Secure Provisioning and Asset Retention
questions.skill: Protecting assets sent for external repair
questions.performanceIndicator: Maintain data protection and custody when hardware leaves organizational control for maintenance
questions.scenarioContext: A news organization must return a malfunctioning workstation under warranty. The device contains nonremovable storage that held embargoed investigative material, and the vendor may replace rather than return the original unit.
questions.prompt: What is the MOST appropriate action before releasing the workstation?

choices.A: Send the workstation immediately because the warranty agreement establishes vendor ownership during repair.
choices.B: Delete visible files and rely on the vendor's standard intake process.
choices.C: Apply the approved media-handling procedure, including verified sanitization when feasible or an authorized exception with controlled custody.
choices.D: Ask the reporter who used the workstation to decide whether the remaining information is sensitive.

questions.explanation: An asset leaving organizational control requires treatment based on its data sensitivity and the ability to sanitize the media. Verified sanitization is preferred; if it is infeasible, an authorized exception and controlled custody are needed. Warranty status does not transfer accountability, ordinary deletion may leave remanent data, and the individual user should not replace the approved process.

questions.competency: II.B — Secure Provisioning and Asset Retention
questions.skill: Coordinating secure employee onboarding
questions.performanceIndicator: Provision personnel, access, equipment, and accountability from an approved role and start date
questions.scenarioContext: A biotechnology startup frequently prepares new employees by copying the access and equipment assignments of whoever previously held a similar title. Managers do not confirm current duties, and accounts sometimes become active days before the employee's start date.
questions.prompt: Which change would provide the STRONGEST provisioning control?

choices.A: Continue copying prior assignments but require the new employee to report unnecessary access.
choices.B: Activate every account early so managers can test the employee's access before arrival.
choices.C: Use job titles as the sole basis for all access and equipment decisions.
choices.D: Require manager-approved role needs, effective dates, least-privilege access, and documented receipt of assigned assets.

questions.explanation: Secure onboarding begins with current, approved job needs and coordinates activation timing, least privilege, and accountable asset assignment. Copying another person's profile can reproduce obsolete or excessive permissions. Early activation creates avoidable exposure, and job titles alone may not reflect actual responsibilities.

questions.competency: II.B — Secure Provisioning and Asset Retention
questions.skill: Resolving conflicting record-retention requirements
questions.performanceIndicator: Use authoritative review to establish a defensible retention period when obligations differ
questions.scenarioContext: An international shipping company finds that a contract requires certain transaction records to be kept for four years, while an applicable regulation requires the same records for seven years. The business unit would prefer two years to reduce storage cost.
questions.prompt: Which retention period should the records owner adopt?

choices.A: Two years, because the business unit owns the operational budget
choices.B: Seven years, after confirming applicability and documenting the controlling requirement
choices.C: Four years, because a signed contract is more specific than a regulation
choices.D: Indefinitely, because conflicting periods make scheduled disposition unsafe

questions.explanation: After confirming that both requirements apply, the organization must satisfy the longer mandatory period and document the basis for the schedule. Cost preference cannot shorten a binding obligation, the contract does not negate the regulation, and indefinite retention adds risk beyond the stated requirements without justification.

questions.competency: II.B — Secure Provisioning and Asset Retention
questions.skill: Preserving retention metadata during records migration
questions.performanceIndicator: Validate content, ownership, retention dates, and disposition rules before retiring a legacy repository
questions.scenarioContext: A public utility is migrating records to a new document platform. The migration team has copied the files but omitted creation dates, owner assignments, legal-hold indicators, and scheduled disposition dates from its test conversion.
questions.prompt: What should happen before the legacy platform is retired?

choices.A: Validate and migrate the governance metadata needed to preserve retention, ownership, and hold requirements.
choices.B: Reset every migrated record to a new full retention period beginning on the migration date.
choices.C: Retain the legacy platform permanently as the only source of recordkeeping metadata.
choices.D: Let users recreate metadata only when they next open a migrated record.

questions.explanation: A records migration must preserve the metadata that makes retention, ownership, holds, and defensible disposition enforceable. Restarting every retention period creates unnecessary over-retention, preserving the old platform indefinitely avoids rather than solves the migration problem, and user reconstruction would be incomplete and inconsistent.

questions.competency: II.C — The Data Lifecycle and Data Security Controls
questions.skill: Controlling data copies created by snapshots
questions.performanceIndicator: Extend classification, access, inventory, and disposition controls to secondary stored copies
questions.scenarioContext: A property-management company regularly clones production databases for troubleshooting. The temporary environments are deleted, but their storage snapshots remain for years, retain production classifications, and are accessible to a larger administrator group than the source systems.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST corrective action?

choices.A: Keep the snapshots because deleting the temporary environments removes the primary exposure.
choices.B: Rename the snapshots so administrators understand that they are no longer active.
choices.C: Inventory the snapshots as data copies, restrict access, and apply approved retention and secure disposition requirements.
choices.D: Transfer all snapshots to lower-cost storage without changing permissions or retention.

questions.explanation: Snapshots remain data assets even after the associated environment is removed. They must be inventoried, protected according to classification, retained only as required, and securely disposed of when no longer needed. Renaming or moving them does not reduce unauthorized access or over-retention, and environment deletion does not eliminate the copied data.

questions.competency: II.C — The Data Lifecycle and Data Security Controls
questions.skill: Selecting a data protection standard from business requirements
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose and tailor a standard based on asset classification, lifecycle, obligations, and operating context
questions.scenarioContext: A global agricultural company is selecting a data protection standard for research data used in laboratories, shared with universities, stored in cloud services, and archived for patent support. One team recommends adopting whichever standard is easiest for its current tools to implement.
questions.prompt: Which selection approach is MOST appropriate?

choices.A: Select the least costly standard and address uncovered risks after incidents occur.
choices.B: Derive requirements from classification, lifecycle uses, applicable obligations, and risk, then scope and tailor the selected controls.
choices.C: Use the laboratory team's preferred controls for every environment without modification.
choices.D: Allow each external university to define the company's protection standard.

questions.explanation: The standard should be driven by the information's classification, lifecycle, legal and contractual obligations, operating environments, and risk. Scoping and tailoring then adapt controls while preserving required outcomes. Tool convenience, one environment's preferences, or external recipients alone should not define enterprise protection requirements.

questions.competency: II.C — The Data Lifecycle and Data Security Controls
questions.skill: Choosing destruction methods for different media types
questions.performanceIndicator: Match physical destruction and purging techniques to media technology and final disposition
questions.scenarioContext: A recording studio is retiring write-once optical discs containing unreleased material and reusable magnetic tapes containing restricted project backups. Both media sets will leave organizational custody; the tapes support an approved purge technique and will be resold.
questions.prompt: Which TWO disposition decisions are most appropriate? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Physically destroy the optical discs with an approved process that renders their data unrecoverable.
choices.B: Clear the optical discs by deleting their directory entries before recycling.
choices.C: Relabel the magnetic tapes as blank without performing sanitization.
choices.D: Purge and verify the magnetic tapes using the approved technique before resale.
choices.E: Retain both media sets indefinitely because external disposition cannot be made risk-free.

questions.explanation: Write-once optical media intended for disposal should be physically destroyed using an approved process. Reusable magnetic tapes leaving custody may be purged with a supported, approved technique and verified before resale. Deleting directory entries or relabeling media does not address remanence, while indefinite retention creates continuing exposure without a business need.

questions.competency: II.C — The Data Lifecycle and Data Security Controls
questions.skill: Mapping data flows before control selection
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify lifecycle stages, copies, transfers, owners, and disposition points to establish complete control coverage
questions.scenarioContext: A benefits administrator wants to strengthen protection for enrollment data. Interviews reveal that information moves from a web form to a processing service, reporting warehouse, support queue, partner feed, and archive, but no complete flow or copy inventory exists.
questions.prompt: What should the security architect do FIRST?

choices.A: Purchase a data protection product that covers the web form and expand it later.
choices.B: Protect only the archive because it contains the longest-lived copy.
choices.C: Ask each system administrator to select controls independently for the local copy.
choices.D: Map the end-to-end data lifecycle, including copies, transfers, ownership, access, retention, and destruction points.

questions.explanation: A complete lifecycle and data-flow map establishes where the information exists, how it moves, who is accountable, and where controls and disposition must apply. Product selection before understanding scope may leave major gaps. Focusing on one copy or delegating disconnected local decisions cannot provide consistent end-to-end protection.

questions.competency: II.C — The Data Lifecycle and Data Security Controls
questions.skill: Controlling sensitive data in nonproduction use
questions.performanceIndicator: Reduce exposure by substituting protected test data when full production values are unnecessary
questions.scenarioContext: A university's application team copies complete student records into a testing environment to reproduce software defects. Testers need realistic formats and relationships, but they do not need actual student identities or contact details.
questions.prompt: Which control BEST supports the testing requirement while reducing exposure?

choices.A: Continue using complete records because the testers are employees.
choices.B: Move the testing environment to a separate network while leaving the data unchanged.
choices.C: Use appropriately de-identified, tokenized, or synthetic test data that preserves required formats and relationships.
choices.D: Archive the production records immediately after each test cycle.

questions.explanation: Protected or synthetic test data can preserve the structure needed for testing without exposing unnecessary real identities. Employment status does not create a need for complete records. Network separation is useful but does not minimize the copied data, and archiving after use does not prevent exposure during the test cycle.

questions.competency: III.A — Secure Design Principles, Security Models, Control Selection, and System Security Capabilities
questions.skill: Applying the Clark-Wilson integrity model to financial transactions
questions.performanceIndicator: Select an integrity architecture based on constrained procedures and independent validation
questions.scenarioContext: A payroll platform must prevent users from directly changing salary records. All changes must use approved procedures, preserve an audit trail, and be independently reconciled against authorized requests.
questions.prompt: Which formal security model MOST directly supports this design?

choices.A: Bell-LaPadula, because its primary objective is to prevent disclosure across classification levels
choices.B: Brewer-Nash, because it dynamically separates access to competing organizations' data
choices.C: Clark-Wilson, because it protects integrity through well-formed transactions and separation of duties
choices.D: Biba, because it requires every business transaction to be approved by two named users

questions.explanation: Clark-Wilson protects commercial data integrity through constrained data items, authorized transformation procedures, auditing, and separation of duties. Bell-LaPadula focuses on confidentiality, while Brewer-Nash addresses conflicts of interest. Biba is an integrity model, but it does not specifically define the well-formed transaction and certification mechanisms described here.

questions.competency: III.A — Secure Design Principles, Security Models, Control Selection, and System Security Capabilities
questions.skill: Applying noninterference to multilevel processing
questions.performanceIndicator: Recognize when high-level activity must not influence low-level observable behavior
questions.scenarioContext: A defense analytics system processes restricted and public workloads on the same platform. Architects require that changes in restricted processing must not alter outputs or observable behavior available to public users.
questions.prompt: Which security-model concept BEST expresses this requirement?

choices.A: Noninterference
choices.B: Aggregation
choices.C: Least functionality
choices.D: Open design

questions.explanation: Noninterference requires actions at a higher security level not to affect what lower-level users can observe, reducing unintended information flow. Aggregation concerns the sensitivity created by combining data. Least functionality reduces unnecessary features, and open design avoids relying on design secrecy; neither directly states the required flow property.

questions.competency: III.A — Secure Design Principles, Security Models, Control Selection, and System Security Capabilities
questions.skill: Reducing attack surface through simple architecture
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose a design that removes unnecessary components and privilege paths
questions.scenarioContext: A warehouse kiosk needs to run one inventory application. The proposed build includes a general-purpose desktop environment, multiple unused services, local development tools, and permanent administrator access for operators.
questions.prompt: Which redesign BEST follows the principles of keeping security simple and minimizing functionality?

choices.A: Retain the full desktop build and rely on annual vulnerability scans to identify excess services.
choices.B: Keep development tools installed but hide their shortcuts from kiosk users.
choices.C: Allow operators to retain administrator rights so they can resolve application failures quickly.
choices.D: Use a minimal locked-down image that runs only required services and separates maintenance privileges from routine use.

questions.explanation: A minimal locked-down image removes unnecessary code and services while separating privileged maintenance from normal operation, directly reducing attack surface and complexity. Scanning a broad build does not eliminate its exposure. Hidden tools remain installed, and permanent administrator access increases the impact of misuse or compromise.

questions.competency: III.A — Secure Design Principles, Security Models, Control Selection, and System Security Capabilities
questions.skill: Using a trusted platform module for measured boot attestation
questions.performanceIndicator: Match platform-integrity evidence to hardware-rooted measurement capabilities
questions.scenarioContext: A lender wants managed laptops to prove that approved firmware and boot components loaded before the laptops receive access to a sensitive application. The evidence must be resistant to software-only tampering.
questions.prompt: Which capability is the MOST appropriate foundation for this requirement?

choices.A: Full-disk encryption using a password entered after the operating system starts
choices.B: Trusted platform module measurements and remote attestation tied to the boot sequence
choices.C: Application logging stored in a writable local directory
choices.D: A network inventory record containing the laptop model and assigned user

questions.explanation: A trusted platform module can protect boot measurements and support attestation so a relying service can evaluate platform state against an approved baseline. Full-disk encryption protects stored data but does not by itself prove the boot chain. Writable logs and inventory records are not hardware-rooted evidence of loaded components.

questions.competency: III.A — Secure Design Principles, Security Models, Control Selection, and System Security Capabilities
questions.skill: Deriving control selection from system security requirements
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify controls that directly implement stated confidentiality and availability needs
questions.scenarioContext: An emergency coordination system has two approved requirements: sensitive plans must remain unreadable if storage media are removed, and dispatch functions must continue after the loss of one processing node.
questions.prompt: Which TWO controls MOST directly implement the stated requirements? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Role-based access restrictions for users viewing plans on an operating system
choices.B: Encryption of stored plans with protected key management
choices.C: Daily backups stored on the same processing node as the dispatch service
choices.D: Physical access controls around the primary equipment room
choices.E: Redundant processing nodes with tested failover

questions.explanation: Storage encryption with protected keys directly addresses media confidentiality, while redundant nodes with tested failover address the stated single-node availability requirement. User access restrictions and equipment-room controls do not protect removed media cryptographically. A backup on the failed node cannot maintain dispatch processing after that node is lost.

questions.competency: III.B — Vulnerabilities Across Modern Architectures
questions.skill: Protecting sensitive data processed on client systems
questions.performanceIndicator: Minimize local exposure while preserving necessary offline operation
questions.scenarioContext: Field inspectors use a desktop client that downloads an entire regulated customer database to each laptop, although an inspector needs only assigned records for one day of offline work. Several laptops have recently been lost.
questions.prompt: Which architectural change BEST reduces the client-side exposure?

choices.A: Require stronger user authentication but retain the entire unencrypted database on every laptop.
choices.B: Increase synchronization frequency while keeping every customer record on each laptop.
choices.C: Move the cache to a separate local partition but allow the application to store it unencrypted.
choices.D: Provide only assigned records, encrypt protected local storage, and remove cached data when the offline need ends.

questions.explanation: Limiting downloads to assigned records applies data minimization, while protected local storage and time-bound removal reduce the consequence of device loss. Renaming a directory is obscurity. More frequent synchronization does not reduce the local dataset, and an unencrypted partition offers no meaningful confidentiality improvement.

questions.competency: III.B — Vulnerabilities Across Modern Architectures
questions.skill: Preventing credential exposure in reusable cloud images
questions.performanceIndicator: Separate secrets from machine images and control image promotion
questions.scenarioContext: A software company creates reusable virtual-machine images for an infrastructure cloud. A review finds static service credentials, deployment tokens, and private keys embedded in the images before they are copied into several accounts.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST architectural remediation?

choices.A: Encrypt each image with one shared key and leave the embedded credentials unchanged.
choices.B: Build credential-free images, scan them before promotion, and obtain short-lived secrets from an authorized service at deployment time.
choices.C: Restrict image names to administrators while retaining the same embedded keys across accounts.
choices.D: Rotate the embedded credentials more frequently while continuing to place them in every shared image.

questions.explanation: Credential-free images prevent secrets from propagating with every copy, while controlled scanning and short-lived deployment-time retrieval reduce persistence and scope. Encrypting an image does not solve credential reuse after launch. Restricted names do not protect image contents, and frequent rotation still distributes each new secret across every image copy.

questions.competency: III.B — Vulnerabilities Across Modern Architectures
questions.skill: Reducing database inference risk from aggregate queries
questions.performanceIndicator: Select query controls that limit deduction of individual records
questions.scenarioContext: A workforce analytics database blocks direct access to individual salaries but allows users to run unlimited aggregate queries. Analysts can vary one filter at a time and subtract results to infer a specific employee's salary.
questions.prompt: Which control strategy BEST addresses the vulnerability?

choices.A: Enforce minimum result-set sizes, restrict overlapping queries, and monitor patterns that can reveal individual values.
choices.B: Mask displayed averages to fewer decimal places but continue allowing overlapping result sets.
choices.C: Permit aggregate queries only during business hours without limiting query combinations.
choices.D: Allow unrestricted aggregates but require users to acknowledge a confidentiality notice once per year.

questions.explanation: Minimum group sizes, controls on closely overlapping queries, and pattern monitoring make differencing and inference attacks more difficult. Rounding can still leave exploitable differences, and limiting query hours does not restrict revealing combinations. An acknowledgment is an administrative measure that does not prevent inference.

questions.competency: III.B — Vulnerabilities Across Modern Architectures
questions.skill: Preserving independence of industrial safety functions
questions.performanceIndicator: Prevent common-mode compromise between production control and safety systems
questions.scenarioContext: A chemical processing plant proposes placing its safety instrumented system on the same controllers, administrative workstations, and update process as the basic production control system to reduce cost.
questions.prompt: Which security architecture recommendation is MOST appropriate?

choices.A: Place the shared production and safety controllers in a restricted cabinet while retaining common software and administration.
choices.B: Use the same administrator account so emergency maintenance remains simple.
choices.C: Maintain justified independence for safety functions, with controlled interfaces and separate failure and compromise paths.
choices.D: Connect both systems directly to business applications to simplify status reporting.

questions.explanation: Independent safety functions with controlled interfaces reduce common-mode failures and help preserve the safety system if production controls are compromised. Screen colors provide no isolation. Shared administration increases common dependency, and direct business connectivity expands attack paths into both environments.

questions.competency: III.B — Vulnerabilities Across Modern Architectures
questions.skill: Reducing isolation risk in virtual-machine hosting
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify controls that reduce cross-tenant and device-passthrough exposure
questions.scenarioContext: A research cloud will host highly sensitive analysis beside lower-trust workloads. Some tenants request direct hardware-device passthrough for performance, and management is concerned about isolation failure and residual exposure.
questions.prompt: Which TWO controls BEST address the stated architectural risks? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Place the most sensitive workloads on dedicated hosts or equivalently strong isolation boundaries based on risk.
choices.B: Use one privileged host account for all tenant support personnel.
choices.C: Allow unrestricted device passthrough whenever a workload requests higher performance.
choices.D: Limit hardware passthrough to approved cases and enforce input-output memory isolation supported by the platform.
choices.E: Retain previous tenants' memory snapshots to accelerate future troubleshooting.

questions.explanation: Dedicated or comparably strong boundaries reduce co-residency risk for highly sensitive workloads, while controlled passthrough with input-output memory isolation limits device access to host memory. Shared privileged accounts weaken accountability. Unrestricted passthrough expands exposure, and retaining tenant memory can disclose residual sensitive data.

questions.competency: III.C — Cryptographic Solutions and Cryptanalytic Attacks
questions.skill: Evaluating resistance to brute-force key search
questions.performanceIndicator: Recognize the role of effective key-space size in exhaustive search
questions.prompt: Assuming a sound symmetric algorithm with no shortcut attack, which change MOST directly increases resistance to brute-force key search?

choices.A: Encoding the ciphertext in a different printable format
choices.B: Increasing the effective key length while maintaining secure key generation
choices.C: Renaming the algorithm in system documentation
choices.D: Dividing the same ciphertext into smaller files

questions.explanation: A larger effective key space increases the number of candidate keys an attacker must test, assuming the algorithm and key generation remain sound. Re-encoding or splitting ciphertext does not change the cryptographic work factor. Renaming an algorithm has no technical effect.

questions.competency: III.C — Cryptographic Solutions and Cryptanalytic Attacks
questions.skill: Selecting authenticated encryption for protected records
questions.performanceIndicator: Choose a construction that provides confidentiality and detects unauthorized modification
questions.scenarioContext: A clinical device stores records that must remain confidential and must be rejected if an attacker alters their encrypted representation. The design team can use a supported authenticated-encryption construction.
questions.prompt: Which approach BEST satisfies both requirements?

choices.A: Encrypt the records without an integrity mechanism and rely on file timestamps.
choices.B: Hash the plaintext and store both the plaintext and hash together without a secret key.
choices.C: Encode the records before storage and restrict knowledge of the encoding format.
choices.D: Use authenticated encryption with correctly managed keys and unique nonces as required by the construction.

questions.explanation: Authenticated encryption provides confidentiality and verifies ciphertext integrity when keys and nonces are managed according to the construction. Encryption alone may not detect malicious modification. An unkeyed hash stored with plaintext can be replaced, and encoding offers neither cryptographic confidentiality nor integrity.

questions.competency: III.C — Cryptographic Solutions and Cryptanalytic Attacks
questions.skill: Separating encryption-key recovery from signing-key custody
questions.performanceIndicator: Design recovery controls without undermining signature accountability
questions.scenarioContext: A consulting firm wants business records to remain recoverable when an employee leaves. A proposal would escrow both employees' data-encryption private keys and their private digital-signature keys with the same recovery team.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST security-architecture recommendation?

choices.A: Escrow all private keys together because encryption and signing serve the same security objective.
choices.B: Discard every encryption key at employee departure and rely on retained ciphertext for recovery.
choices.C: Provide controlled recovery for encryption keys when required, but do not escrow personal signing keys in a way that permits others to impersonate the signer.
choices.D: Publish signing private keys after employee departure so reviewers can verify archived signatures.

questions.explanation: Business recovery may justify controlled escrow or recovery of encryption keys, but access to a person's signing private key could enable impersonation and undermine accountability. Encryption and signing have different objectives. Destroying needed decryption keys defeats recovery, while publishing a signing private key destroys its secrecy and trustworthiness.

questions.competency: III.C — Cryptographic Solutions and Cryptanalytic Attacks
questions.skill: Recognizing frequency-analysis attacks
questions.performanceIndicator: Classify cryptanalysis based on recurring symbol patterns
questions.scenarioContext: An examiner studies a large body of ciphertext from a simple substitution scheme and compares recurring symbols and symbol groups with expected patterns in the underlying language.
questions.prompt: Which attack method is the examiner using?

choices.A: Frequency analysis
choices.B: Brute-force key search
choices.C: Side-channel analysis
choices.D: Chosen-ciphertext analysis

questions.explanation: Frequency analysis uses the statistical occurrence of symbols or groups to infer plaintext structure, especially against simple substitution schemes. Brute force tests candidate keys. Side-channel analysis exploits implementation leakage, and chosen-ciphertext analysis relies on access to decryption behavior for selected ciphertexts.

questions.competency: III.C — Cryptographic Solutions and Cryptanalytic Attacks
questions.skill: Preventing nonce reuse in authenticated encryption
questions.performanceIndicator: Select a nonce-generation design that preserves cryptographic security assumptions
questions.scenarioContext: A telemetry platform uses an authenticated-encryption algorithm whose security requires a nonce never to repeat under the same key. Devices currently reset a local counter after every reboot while retaining the same encryption key.
questions.prompt: Which redesign BEST addresses the vulnerability?

choices.A: Keep the rebooting counter but increase the length of the plaintext messages.
choices.B: Use a nonce-generation scheme that guarantees uniqueness for the key, preserves state safely across reboots, or rotates the key before reuse can occur.
choices.C: Reuse a prior nonce only for messages classified as low sensitivity.
choices.D: Encode each repeated nonce before sending it with the ciphertext.

questions.explanation: The design must preserve nonce uniqueness for each key across device restarts or change the key before a nonce can repeat. Message length does not repair nonce reuse. Sensitivity labels do not change the algorithm's security requirements, and encoding a repeated nonce does not make it cryptographically unique.

questions.competency: III.D — Site and Facility Security, and the Information System Lifecycle
questions.skill: Protecting equipment rooms from water damage
questions.performanceIndicator: Select layered controls for plumbing and leak exposure
questions.scenarioContext: A company plans to place a network equipment room below restrooms and beside a domestic-water riser. The room contains critical switching equipment and has no floor-level leak detection.
questions.prompt: Which design response is MOST appropriate before construction approval?

choices.A: Use water-resistant equipment enclosures while leaving the utility source and drainage design unassessed.
choices.B: Raise the equipment racks but omit leak detection and an emergency water-shutoff procedure.
choices.C: Relocate the room or reroute water sources where feasible, then add leak detection, drainage, and protected equipment placement based on residual risk.
choices.D: Move the critical switches higher in the same room without changing the water source or drainage path.

questions.explanation: Avoiding or rerouting the hazard is strongest; leak detection, drainage, and protected equipment placement then reduce residual exposure. Enclosures or elevated racks alone leave detection, shutoff, and drainage gaps. Raising only the switches reduces one exposure but leaves the underlying facility hazard largely unchanged.

questions.competency: III.D — Site and Facility Security, and the Information System Lifecycle
questions.skill: Designing effective perimeter video surveillance
questions.performanceIndicator: Coordinate camera coverage, lighting, retention, and monitoring with response capability
questions.scenarioContext: A distribution center has perimeter cameras, but nighttime glare obscures faces, several fence corners are outside coverage, and recorded alerts are rarely reviewed until days later.
questions.prompt: Which improvement BEST addresses the combined weaknesses?

choices.A: Redesign camera placement and lighting to remove blind spots and glare, then integrate alert monitoring, retention, and response procedures.
choices.B: Increase recording resolution while preserving blind spots and the existing lighting configuration.
choices.C: Retain footage longer but continue reviewing alerts only after unrelated incidents occur.
choices.D: Add warning signs and increase guard patrol frequency while leaving the camera blind spots and lighting problems unchanged.

questions.explanation: Effective surveillance requires usable images, complete risk-based coverage, timely monitoring, appropriate retention, and a response process. Resolution alone cannot capture an area outside the camera view or correct severe glare. Longer retention improves evidence availability but not detection, while warning signs cannot replace the perimeter and surveillance controls.

questions.competency: III.D — Site and Facility Security, and the Information System Lifecycle
questions.skill: Securing receiving and loading areas
questions.performanceIndicator: Identify design controls that prevent deliveries from bypassing protected facility boundaries
questions.scenarioContext: A media archive receives equipment and supplies through a loading dock that opens into the same corridor used to enter restricted storage rooms. Deliveries are often left unattended before employees claim them.
questions.prompt: Which TWO changes BEST reduce the loading-area risk? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Allow delivery drivers to place shipments directly inside restricted storage rooms during busy periods.
choices.B: Use the loading dock as an alternate employee entrance whenever the lobby is crowded.
choices.C: Separate the receiving zone from restricted areas with controlled doors and defined movement paths.
choices.D: Remove delivery records after packages are claimed to reduce administrative storage.
choices.E: Verify, inspect, log, and secure deliveries until an authorized recipient accepts them.

questions.explanation: A controlled receiving boundary prevents the dock from becoming a direct path into restricted areas, while verification, inspection, logging, and secure holding preserve accountability for deliveries. Direct driver access and use as an informal employee entrance bypass zoning. Removing delivery records weakens traceability.

questions.competency: III.D — Site and Facility Security, and the Information System Lifecycle
questions.skill: Maintaining accountability for physical keys
questions.performanceIndicator: Respond to an unaccounted master key with risk-based rekeying and stronger custody controls
questions.scenarioContext: During an access review, a laboratory cannot account for a master key that opens several sensitive rooms. The key has no unique marking, and the sign-out sheet does not show who last held it.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST response?

choices.A: Issue additional copies so authorized staff are less likely to borrow the missing key.
choices.B: Wait for evidence of unauthorized entry before changing locks or procedures.
choices.C: Update the sign-out sheet but assume the missing key is still inside the facility.
choices.D: Assess affected doors, rekey or replace compromised cylinders as risk requires, and implement uniquely tracked key custody.

questions.explanation: A missing master key creates an unresolved access path, so affected locks must be evaluated and changed according to risk while stronger issuance and custody records prevent recurrence. More copies increase exposure. Waiting leaves sensitive rooms vulnerable, and paperwork alone cannot neutralize a key that may be outside organizational control.

questions.competency: III.D — Site and Facility Security, and the Information System Lifecycle
questions.skill: Protecting systems during a facility relocation
questions.performanceIndicator: Preserve custody, environmental protection, and verified control restoration during a move
questions.scenarioContext: A regional office is moving servers and backup media to a new facility. A general moving company will transport equipment, and the new room's access controls and environmental monitoring have not yet been acceptance-tested.
questions.prompt: Which relocation plan BEST protects the systems throughout the lifecycle transition?

choices.A: Ship all equipment immediately and validate the new room after production resumes.
choices.B: Inventory and seal assets, maintain documented custody with authorized transport, and verify new-site physical and environmental controls before installation.
choices.C: Allow the mover to create the asset list after delivery so the organization does not duplicate effort.
choices.D: Record serial numbers but use standard transport without sealed packaging or documented custody handoffs.

questions.explanation: A verified inventory, tamper-evident protection, controlled custody, authorized transport, and pre-installation acceptance testing preserve accountability and ensure the destination is ready. Shipping before validation risks damage or exposure. Delegating the inventory weakens organizational control, while serial numbers without sealed transport and recorded custody do not adequately protect the move.

questions.competency: IV.A — Network Architecture Fundamentals
questions.skill: Resolving overlapping private IP address spaces
questions.performanceIndicator: Select a controlled connectivity design when two networks use conflicting address ranges
questions.scenarioContext: After an acquisition, two companies must exchange a limited set of application flows, but both use the same private IPv4 address ranges. Immediate enterprise-wide renumbering is not feasible.
questions.prompt: Which solution BEST enables the required connectivity while limiting security impact?

choices.A: Bridge the two networks at Layer 2 and permit duplicate addresses to coexist.
